ui.categoryCallout: Before you buy on sale, check what a good price per GB looks like:

microsd-value.label: microSD, budget A1/A2 (UHS-I)
microsd-value.note: Fine for game libraries and basic 1080p cameras. Check for a V30 or U3 mark before using one in a 4K camera.

microsd-v30.label: microSD, V30 A2 (UHS-I)
microsd-v30.note: The default card for drones, action cameras and handhelds.

microsd-express.label: microSD Express
microsd-express.note: Required for Switch 2 game storage. Runs at UHS-I speed in other devices.

microsd-uhs2.label: microSD, UHS-II V60
microsd-uhs2.note: Only faster in a UHS-II slot or reader. In a UHS-I device it performs like a V30 card.

sd-v30.label: SD, V30 (UHS-I)
sd-v30.note: Full speed in UHS-I cameras such as the Canon EOS R50 and Fujifilm X100V.

sd-v60.label: SD, UHS-II V60
sd-v60.note: Clears burst buffers faster in UHS-II cameras and handles most 4K modes.

sd-v90.label: SD, UHS-II V90
sd-v90.note: For cameras that list V90 for their top video modes, such as high-bitrate 4K All-I.

cfexpress-b.label: CFexpress Type B
cfexpress-b.note: Only for cameras with a Type B slot, such as the Canon EOS R5 and Nikon Z8.

cfexpress-a.label: CFexpress Type A
cfexpress-a.note: Only for Sony bodies with a Type A slot, such as the A7 IV, FX3 and A1. Type B cards do not fit.

hub.title: SD Card Deals for Black Friday 2026: Price per GB | SD Card Checker
hub.metaDescription: What a good Black Friday price per GB looks like for microSD, microSD Express, SD and CFexpress cards, and which card to buy for your console, drone or camera.
hub.h1: SD card deals: what a good price per GB looks like
intro: A sale price is a deal only when the price per GB beats what the card usually costs. Divide the price by the capacity in GB: a $40 512GB card costs $0.078 per GB.
Black Friday is November 27, 2026 and Cyber Monday is November 30. Amazon prices can change during the sale, so check the price per GB again at checkout.
hub.rulesHeading: How to judge a memory card deal
rules: Compare at the same capacity. Price per GB drops as capacity rises, then climbs again at the newest sizes: 1.5TB and 2TB cards usually cost more per GB than 1TB.
Check the exact model. SanDisk Ultra is rated U1 and SanDisk Extreme is rated V30. Listings look alike, so a cheap Ultra is not an Extreme deal.
Ignore the headline read speed. "Up to 190 MB/s" is a peak read figure. The speed class (U3, V30, V60, V90) is the minimum sustained write, which is what video recording needs.
Don't pay for speed your slot can't use. A UHS-II card runs at UHS-I speed in a UHS-I slot, and UHS-I tops out at 104 MB/s.
Check the seller. Buy cards shipped and sold by Amazon.com or by the brand's own Amazon store.
hub.avoidHeading: Fake cards are the main risk in a sale
avoid: Fake cards report a capacity they don't have. Once the real capacity fills, they overwrite earlier files without a warning.
An unknown-brand 1TB or 2TB microSD priced below a name-brand 256GB card is a fake.
Test every new card with H2testw (Windows) or F3 (macOS and Linux) before you record anything you can't reshoot.

faq.q: Is Black Friday a good time to buy an SD card?
faq.a: Yes, when the price per GB lands at or below the range for that card type. A crossed-out list price on its own does not prove a deal, so compare price per GB at the same capacity.

faq.q: How do I calculate SD card price per GB?
faq.a: Divide the price by the capacity in GB. $80 for a 1TB card is $0.08 per GB, since card labels count 1TB as 1,000GB.

faq.q: Are cheap 1TB and 2TB microSD cards on Amazon fake?
faq.a: Unknown-brand ones priced below a name-brand 256GB card are. Buy SanDisk, Samsung, Lexar or Kingston cards shipped and sold by Amazon.com or the brand's store, and run H2testw or F3 on every new card.

faq.q: Should I buy a bigger card on sale or a faster one?
faq.a: Bigger, for consoles, handhelds, drones and action cameras. Their slots are UHS-I, which caps speed at 104 MB/s. Cameras with UHS-II slots are the exception: buy the speed class the camera lists for its video modes first.

pages.hubBlurb: A2 microSD cards for game libraries. Spend the sale money on capacity.
pages.title: Steam Deck and Switch SD Card Deals: Price per GB | SD Card Checker
pages.metaDescription: Black Friday microSD guide for Steam Deck, Switch, ROG Ally and Legion Go: a good price per GB for A2 cards, which size to buy, and how to avoid fake cards.
intro: Steam Deck, Nintendo Switch, ROG Ally and Legion Go load games from microSD in small random reads, so an A2 UHS-I card from a known brand covers nearly every handheld. On sale, spend the money on capacity: 512GB or 1TB holds a large game library.
Buying for a Switch 2? It needs a microSD Express card, which has its own Switch 2 deals guide.
capacity: Steam Deck, ROG Ally and Legion Go: 512GB or 1TB. Large PC games take 50GB to 150GB each.
Nintendo Switch, Switch OLED and Switch Lite: 256GB or 512GB. Most Switch games are under 20GB.
Retro handhelds (Anbernic, Miyoo, R36S): 64GB to 128GB holds cartridge-era ROM sets. Retroid and AYN devices that run disc-based games need 256GB or more, since each disc image takes 1GB to 8GB.
avoid: UHS-II and V60 cards for a Steam Deck, Switch or original Legion Go. Those slots are UHS-I, so you pay for speed the device never uses.
Standard microSD cards for Switch 2 game storage. Switch 2 only accepts microSD Express for games.
Class 10 or U1 cards with no A1 or A2 rating. Game loading depends on random reads, which the A ratings cover.
Unknown-brand 1TB and 2TB cards priced below a name-brand 256GB card.

faq.q: What is a good Black Friday price for a 1TB microSD card?
faq.a: About $80 to $130 for a V30 A2 card such as the SanDisk Extreme or Samsung PRO Plus, which is $0.08 to $0.13 per GB. Budget A2 cards such as the Samsung EVO Select should come in lower.

faq.q: Do I need a UHS-II card for the ROG Ally or Legion Go 2?
faq.a: No. Both slots accept UHS-II and load games a little faster with it, but UHS-II microSD costs two to three times as much per GB. A 1TB A2 UHS-I card is the better buy for the same money.

faq.q: Will a Switch microSD card work in a Steam Deck?
faq.a: Yes. Both use UHS-I microSD, so the same A2 card works in either. Format it in the device you move it to, since each console uses its own file layout.

pages.hubBlurb: Switch 2 only takes microSD Express for games. What a good Express price looks like.
pages.title: Switch 2 microSD Express Card Deals: Price per GB | SD Card Checker
pages.metaDescription: Switch 2 only stores games on microSD Express cards. What a good Black Friday price per GB looks like for Express cards, which size to buy, and what to skip.
intro: Nintendo Switch 2 only stores games on microSD Express cards. A standard microSD card, even a UHS-II one, does not work for game storage, so a cheap UHS-I deal is the wrong card for this console.
Express cards cost about twice as much per GB as V30 A2 cards, so a sale is a good time to buy one. Look for the microSD Express logo on the card and in the listing photos.
capacity: 256GB doubles the Switch 2's 256GB of built-in storage.
512GB if you buy most games as digital downloads.
1TB and up costs more per GB at Express prices. Buy it only if you already fill 512GB.
avoid: Cards labeled "for Switch" without the microSD Express logo. SanDisk's Zelda, Mario and Pokemon designs are UHS-I cards for the original Switch.
UHS-II microSD cards. They are fast, but Switch 2 does not accept them for games.
Express listings from unknown brands with no logo on the card. Express is new, so fake listings borrow the name.

faq.q: What is a good price for a Switch 2 microSD Express card?
faq.a: About $0.15 to $0.30 per GB on sale, so roughly $40 to $75 for 256GB. Check the per-GB price at 512GB too: larger Express cards are not always cheaper per GB.

faq.q: Can I use a regular microSD card in Switch 2?
faq.a: Not for games. Switch 2 stores games only on microSD Express cards. An old card can go in once to copy Switch screenshots and videos to the console.

faq.q: Will a Switch 2 microSD Express card work in my original Switch?
faq.a: Yes, at UHS-I speed. Express cards are backward compatible with UHS-I slots, so one card can move between consoles.

pages.hubBlurb: V30 microSD in 128GB or 256GB covers DJI Mini, Air and Avata.
pages.title: Drone SD Card Deals: microSD Price per GB for DJI | SD Card Checker
pages.metaDescription: Black Friday microSD guide for DJI Mini, Air, Mavic and Avata drones: V30 cards in 128GB or 256GB, a good price per GB, and which cards to skip.
intro: Most consumer drones, including the DJI Mini, Air and Avata lines, record to a UHS-I microSD card and need a V30 or U3 rating for 4K. A V30 card from SanDisk, Lexar, Kingston or Samsung in 128GB or 256GB covers nearly all of them, so those are the two sizes to watch in a sale.
capacity: 128GB holds about 2.5 hours of 4K at 100 Mbps, more than three batteries of flying on a DJI Mini.
256GB for drones that record at 150 Mbps or more, such as the DJI Mini 4 Pro and Air 3S, or for a trip without a laptop to offload.
512GB rarely pays off. A second 128GB card costs less and splits the risk if one fails.
avoid: Cards without a V30 or U3 rating. A U1 card can drop frames or stop recording in 4K.
Paying UHS-II prices for a UHS-I drone. The drone writes at UHS-I speed; UHS-II only speeds up offloading through a UHS-II reader.
A card for the DJI Neo. It has 22GB of internal storage and no card slot.
Unknown-brand high-capacity cards. A fake card overwrites earlier clips once its real capacity fills, and you won't know until you land.

faq.q: What is a good price for a 256GB microSD card for a DJI drone?
faq.a: About $20 to $33 for a V30 card such as the SanDisk Extreme or Kingston Canvas Go! Plus, which is $0.08 to $0.13 per GB.

faq.q: Do DJI drones need a V60 microSD card?
faq.a: Most don't. DJI asks for UHS-I Speed Grade 3 (U3) or faster on the Mini and Air lines. A V60 card writes no faster in a UHS-I drone and only saves time when you offload through a UHS-II reader.

pages.hubBlurb: V30 microSD for GoPro, DJI Osmo and Insta360. 256GB is the size to buy.
pages.title: GoPro and Action Camera SD Card Deals: Price per GB | SD Card Checker
pages.metaDescription: Black Friday microSD guide for GoPro, DJI Osmo Action, Osmo Pocket and Insta360: V30 cards, a good price per GB, which size to buy and what to avoid.
intro: GoPro, DJI Osmo Action, Osmo Pocket and Insta360 cameras record to UHS-I microSD and need a V30 card for their top 4K and 5K modes. 256GB is the size to buy on sale for most of them.
capacity: 256GB holds about 4.5 hours at the GoPro Hero 13's top 120 Mbps bitrate.
512GB or 1TB for 360 cameras such as the Insta360 X4 and X5, whose 8K files fill a card faster.
128GB is enough for short clips at 1080p or 4K30.
avoid: Cards rated only U1 or Class 10. They can stop recording at high bitrates.
UHS-II cards. Action cameras use UHS-I slots, so pay UHS-I prices.
A card for the Insta360 GO 3. It records to internal storage and has no slot.
Unknown-brand 1TB and 2TB cards priced below a name-brand 256GB card.

faq.q: What size microSD card should I buy for a GoPro on sale?
faq.a: 256GB. It holds about 4.5 hours at the Hero 13's top bitrate, and at $0.08 to $0.13 per GB a V30 card costs about $20 to $33 on sale.

faq.q: Is a V60 card worth it for an action camera?
faq.a: No. GoPro, DJI and Insta360 cameras write to UHS-I slots, where a V30 card keeps up with every recording mode. A V60 card only speeds up offloading through a UHS-II reader.

pages.hubBlurb: SD, UHS-II and CFexpress. Match the card to your camera's slot before buying.
pages.title: Camera SD Card Deals: UHS-II and V90 Price per GB | SD Card Checker
pages.metaDescription: Black Friday SD card guide for mirrorless cameras: what a good price per GB looks like for V30, V60, V90 and CFexpress cards, and which one your camera uses.
intro: Cameras split into two groups. UHS-I bodies such as the Canon EOS R50, Fujifilm X100V and Nikon Z50 II run at full speed on a V30 SD card. UHS-II bodies such as the Sony A6700, Canon EOS R6 Mark II and Fujifilm X-T5 clear bursts faster with a UHS-II V60 or V90 card.
Check your camera's slot type on its device page before buying an expensive card on sale.
capacity: 256GB for 4K video, or RAW files from 40MP and higher sensors.
Two cards, not one big one, in dual-slot bodies: record to both slots for an instant backup.
avoid: V90 cards for a UHS-I camera. The UHS-I bus caps at 104 MB/s, so a V30 card performs the same.
SD cards when your camera's top video modes need CFexpress. The Canon EOS R5 records 8K RAW only to CFexpress Type B.
CFexpress Type B cards for Sony bodies. The A7 IV, FX3 and A1 take Type A, which is a different size.
Unknown-brand cards that claim V90 at V30 prices.

faq.q: What is a good Black Friday price for a 128GB V90 SD card?
faq.a: About $75 to $155 for a SanDisk Extreme PRO UHS-II or Sony TOUGH G, which is $0.60 to $1.20 per GB. V60 cards such as the Lexar Professional 1667x cost about half as much and handle 4K in most mirrorless cameras.

faq.q: Is a CFexpress card worth buying on sale?
faq.a: Only if your camera has a CFexpress slot and you use the modes that need it, such as 8K RAW on the Canon EOS R5. For everything else, a UHS-II SD card costs less per GB.
